question: what data do we have on graduation rates

answer.message:
Here are relevant data areas I found in the local IPEDS files:

**Survey: Graduation Rates**

Outcome dates (unless noted): August 31: 2015 through 2024.

- **Frequently used derived variables (GR) 150% of normal time to complete (4-year, 2-year institutions)**.  
  Entering cohorts: 4-year institutions: 2009 through 2017; 2-year institutions: 2012 through 2020.  
  Example fields: Graduation rate, total cohort; Graduation rate, White, non-Hispanic; Graduation rate, Black, non-Hispanic; Graduation rate, Hispanic.
- **Graduation rate data, 150% of normal time to complete (less-than-2-year institutions)**.  
  Entering cohorts: less-than-2-year institutions: 2012 through 2021.  
  Example fields: Revised Cohort; Exclusions; Still enrolled; No longer enrolled.
- **Graduation rate data, 200% of normal time to complete (4-year, less-than-4-year institutions)**.  
  Entering cohorts: 4-year institutions: 2006; 2008 through 2016; less-than-4-year institutions: 2010; 2012 through 2020.  
  Example fields: 4-year Graduation rate - bachelor's degree within 100% of normal time; 6-year Graduation rate - bachelor's degree within 150% of normal time; 8-year Graduation rate - bachelor's degree within 200% of normal time; Graduation rate - degree/certificate within 100% of normal time.
- **Gender unknown reported in revised cohorts (4-year, less-than-4-year institutions)** — Outcome dates: August 31: 2022; 2023.  
  Entering cohorts: 4-year institutions: 2016; 2017; less-than-4-year institutions: 2019; 2020.  
  Example fields: Cohort type; Grand total; Gender unknown; Another gender.
- **Graduation rate data, 150% of normal time to complete (4-year, 2-year institutions)**.  
  Entering cohorts: 4-year institutions: 2009 through 2018; 2-year institutions: 2012 through 2021.  
  Example fields: Graduation rate status in cohort; Cohort data; U.S. Nonresident men; U.S. Nonresident women.
- **Graduation rate data for Pell Grant and Subsidized Stafford loan recipients, 150% of normal time to complete (4-year, 2-year institutions)** — Outcome dates: August 31: 2016 through 2022.  
  Entering cohorts: 4-year institutions: 2010 through 2016; 2-year institutions: 2013 through 2019.  
  Example fields: Cohort type; Pell Grant recipients - revised cohort; Pell Grant recipients - exclusions; Pell Grant recipients - adjusted cohort (revised minus exclusions).
- **Graduation rate data for Pell Grant and Direct Subsidized Loan recipients, 150% of normal time to complete (4-year, 2-year institutions)** — Outcome dates: August 31: 2023; 2024.  
  Entering cohorts: 4-year institutions: 2017; 2018; 2-year institutions: 2020; 2021.  
  Example fields: Cohort type; Pell Grant recipients - revised cohort; Pell Grant recipients - exclusions; Pell Grant recipients - adjusted cohort (revised minus exclusions).

**Survey: Outcome Measures**

Outcome dates: August 31: 2016.

- **Frequently used derived variables (OM) Award and enrollment rates of degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates**.  
  Entering cohorts: 2008.  
  Example fields: Percent of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates receiving an award - 6 years; Percent of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates receiving an award - 8 years; Percent of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates still enrolled at same institution; Percent of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates enrolled at another institution.

These are codebook and physical-table matches, not confirmation that every institution has reported values. Definitions, populations and available breakdowns can differ by year. This is a bounded topic search, not an exhaustive inventory.

To continue, tell me the institution, data area and years you want to analyze.

description: This table contains the graduation rate status as of August 31, 2015 for the cohort of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in both four year and two year institutions. Data for four year institutions include the number of bachelor degree-seeking students who were enrolled in 2009, the number of bachelor degree seeking students who completed any degree/certificate within 150 percent of normal time, the number who completed a bachelor's degree within 100, 125 or 150 percent on normal time, and the number of bachelor's degree-seeking students who transferred out. Data for students seeking a degree/certificate other than a bachelor's degree are also included for four year institutions. Data for two year institutions include the number of full-time, first-time students who were enrolled in 2012, the number of students who completed any degree/certificate within 100 or 150 percent of normal time and the number of students who transferred out. This table has multiple records per institution. Records are uniquely defined by the variables IPEDS ID (UNITID), and the cohort and graduation status within the cohort (GRTYPE). Each record will contain the above data by gender and race/ethnicity. Note: The number of students who completed a degree/certificate within 100 percent of normal time is not available by race/ethnicity and gender for two year institutions.

Data for four year institutions include the number of bachelor degree-seeking students who were enrolled in 2017, the number of bachelor degree seeking students who completed any degree/certificate within 150 percent of normal time, the number who completed a bachelor's degree within 100, 125 or 150 percent on normal time, and the number of bachelor's degree-seeking students who transferred out. Data for students seeking a degree/certificate other than a bachelor's degree are also included for four year institutions. Data for two year institutions include the number of full-time, first-time students who were enrolled in 2020, the number of students who completed any degree/certificate within 100 or 150 percent of normal time and the number of students who transferred out. This table has multiple records per institution. Records are uniquely defined by the variables IPEDS ID (UNITID), and the cohort and graduation status within the cohort (GRTYPE). Each record will contain the above data by gender and race/ethnicity. Note: The number of students who completed a degree/certificate within 100 percent of normal time is not available by race/ethnicity and gender for two year institutions.

Data for two year and less-than 2-year institutions include the number of full-time, first-time students who were enrolled in 2020, the number of students who completed any degree/certificate 150 percent of normal time. This file has multiple records per institution. Records are uniquely defined by the variables IPEDS ID (UNITID), and the cohort (PSGRTYPE, see frequencies for details). Each record will contain data for each of the financial aid subcohorts.

question: what data do we have on expenses

answer.message:
Here are relevant data areas I found in the local IPEDS files:

**Survey: Finance**

Reporting periods: Fiscal year 2015 through Fiscal year 2024.

- **Frequently used/derived variables Finance (F)**.  
  Example fields: Core expenses, total dollars (GASB); Instruction expenses as a percent of total core expenses (GASB); Research expenses as a percent of total core expenses (GASB); Public service expenses as a percent of total core expenses (GASB).

**Survey: Institutional Characteristics**

Reporting periods (unless noted): Academic year 2015-16 through Academic year 2023-24.

- **Student charges by program (vocational programs)**.  
  Example fields: On campus, other expenses 2020-21; On campus, other expenses 2021-22; On campus, other expenses 2022-23; On campus, other expenses 2023-24.
- **Student charges for academic year programs**.  
  Example fields: On campus, other expenses 2020-21; On campus, other expenses 2021-22; On campus, other expenses 2022-23; On campus, other expenses 2023-24.
- **Branch campus locations listed on College Navigator** — Reporting periods: Academic year 2021-22 through Academic year 2023-24.  
  Example fields: On campus, other expenses 2020-21; On campus, other expenses 2021-22; On campus, other expenses 2022-23; On campus, other expenses 2023-24.

**Survey: Cost**

Reporting periods: Academic year 2024-25.

- **Application fees, tuition and required fees, food and housing for undergraduate and graduate students**.  
  Example fields: On campus, other expenses 2021-22; On campus, other expenses 2022-23; On campus, other expenses 2023-24; On campus, other expenses 2024-25.

**Survey: Academic Libraries**

Reporting periods: 2015-16; 2016-17; 2017-18; 2019-20; Fiscal year 2020; Fiscal year 2021; Fiscal year 2022; Fiscal year 2023; Fiscal year 2024.

- **Frequently used/derived variables Academic library indicators**.  
  Example fields: Physical books as a percent of the total library collection; Physical media as a percent of the total library collection; Digital/Electronic books as a percent of the total library collection; Databases as a percent of the total library collection.

These are codebook and physical-table matches, not confirmation that every institution has reported values. Definitions, populations and available breakdowns can differ by year. This is a bounded topic search, not an exhaustive inventory.

To continue, tell me the institution, data area and years you want to analyze.

Information technology expenses related to instructional activities if the institution separately budgets and expenses information technology resources are included (otherwise these expenses are included in academic support). FASB institutions include actual or allocated costs for operation and maintenance of plant, interest, and depreciation. GASB institutions do not include operation and maintenance of plant or interest, but may, as an option, distribute depreciation expense.

datatype: N
fieldwidth: 3
format: Cont
multirecord: 0
filenumber: 87
sectionnumber: 2
longdescription: Physical books as a percent of the total library collection is derived by dividing the number of physical books (LPBOOKS) by the total library collection and multiplying by 100. Total library collection is the sum of physical books (LPBOOKS) , physical media (LPMEDIA), physical serials (LPSERIA) digital/electronic books (LEBOOKS), digital/electronic databases (LEDATAB), digital/electronic media (LEMEDIA) and digital/electronic serials (LESERIA). Physical and digital/electronic serials were not included prior to 2017. Number of physical books - The number of volumes held in the library collection. Volume is a single physical unit of any printed, typewritten, handwritten, mimeographed, or processed work, distinguished from other units by a separate binding, encasement, portfolio, or other clear distinction, which has been cataloged,classified, and made ready for use, and which is typically the unit used to charge circulation transactions.

Number of digital/electronic books - The number of digital/electronic book units held locally and remote units for which permanent or temporary access rights have been acquired. evidence.title: Student charges for academic year programs
evidence.definition:
surveyorder: 10
surveynumber: 1
survey: Institutional Characteristics
yearcoverage: Academic year 2015-16
tablename: IC2015_AY
tablenumber: 13
tabletitle: Student charges for academic year programs
description: This table contains data on student charges for a full academic year. Institutions that offer primarily academic programs measured in credit hours have a predominant calendar system of semester, quarter, trimester, or 4-1-4 or other academic calendar system report student charges for the full academic year. Student charges on this data file include: average tuition and required fees for both full-time undergraduate and graduate students; per credit hour charges for both part-time undergraduate and graduate students; Typical tuition and required fees for a full-time Doctor's - professional practice student in Chiropractic (D.C. or D.C.M.), Dentistry (D.D.S. or D.M.D.), Law (L.L.B. or J.D.), Medicine (M.D.), Optometry (O.D.), Osteopathic Medicine (D.O), Pharmacy (Pharm.D.), Podiatry (D.P.M., Pod.D., D.P.), or, Veterinary Medicine (D.V.M.), and Law (J.D.). The price of attendance of full-time first-time undergraduates that are made available to the public on College Navigator are included in this table. Price of attendance includes amounts for published tuition and required fees, books and supplies, room and board and other expenses. Estimates for books and supplies, room and board and other expenses are those from the Cost of Attendance report used by the financial aid office in determining financial need.
release: Provisional/final (institutions will not be allowed to revise these data)
release date: October 2016

question: what data do we have on faculty

answer.message:
Here are relevant data areas I found in the local IPEDS files:

**Survey: Human Resources**

Reporting periods (unless noted): Fall 2015 through Fall 2024.

- **Full-time instructional staff, by academic rank, faculty and tenure status (Degree-granting institutions)**.  
  Example fields: Faculty and tenure status; All ranks; Professors; Associate professors.
- **Full-time instructional staff, by faculty and tenure status, academic rank, race/ethnicity, and gender (Degree-granting institutions)**.  
  Example fields: Faculty and tenure status; U.S. Nonresident men; U.S. Nonresident women; Race/ethnicity unknown men.
- **Number of staff by occupational category, faculty and tenure status**.  
  Example fields: Occupation and faculty/tenure status; Faculty and tenure status; Occupation; Institution employees (excluding medical school).
- **Number and salary outlays for full-time nonmedical instructional staff, by gender, and academic rank** — Reporting periods: 2015-16 through 2024-25.  
  Example fields: Academic rank; Instructional staff on 9, 10, 11 or 12 month contract-men; Instructional staff on 9, 10, 11 or 12 month contract-women; Instructional staff on 9, 10, 11 or 12 month contract-total.
- **New hires by occupational category, race/ethnicity, and gender (Degree-granting institutions)**.  
  Example fields: Faculty and tenure status; Old new hire categories that are consitent with new codes; U.S. Nonresident men; U.S. Nonresident women.
- **Number and salary outlays for full-time nonmedical noninstructional staff by occupation** — Reporting periods: 2015-16 through 2024-25.  
  Example fields: Full-time non-instructional staff - number; Full-time non-instructional staff - outlays; Research - number; Research - outlays.
- **Frequently used/derived variables Human resources (HR)**.  
  Example fields: Average salary equated to 9 months of full-time instructional staff - all ranks; Average salary equated to 9 months of full-time instructional staff - professors; Average salary equated to 9 months of full-time instructional staff - associate professors; Average salary equated to 9 months of full-time instructional staff - assistant professors.

**Survey: Fall Enrollment**

Reporting periods: Fall 2015 through Fall 2024.

- **Total entering class, retention rates, and student-to-faculty ratio**.  
  Example fields: Student-to-faculty ratio; Full-time first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate (current year GRS cohort); Total entering students at the undergraduate level, fall 2024; Current year GRS cohort as a percent of entering class.

These are codebook and physical-table matches, not confirmation that every institution has reported values. Definitions, populations and available breakdowns can differ by year. This is a bounded topic search, not an exhaustive inventory.

To continue, tell me the institution, data area and years you want to analyze.

tabletitle: Full-time instructional staff, by academic rank, faculty and tenure status (Degree-granting institutions): Fall 2015
description: This table contains the number of full-time instructional staff on the payroll of the institution as of November 1, by academic rank, faculty and tenure status. This table has multiple records per institution. Each record is uniquely defined by the variables IPEDS ID (UNITID), and the variable FACSTAT which is the combination of faculty status and tenure status (tenured, on tenure track, and not on-tenure track/no tenure system). Staff that are not on-tenure track/no tenure system are also classified by the type of contract (multi-year, continuing or at-will contract, annual contract, and less-than-annual contract). Each record contains counts of staff by academic rank (professors, associate professors, etc.) . These data are applicable to degree-granting institutions with 15 or more full-time employees and related administrative offices.

longdescription: Instructional Staff is an occupational category that is comprised of staff who are either: 1) Primarily Instruction or 2) Instruction combined with research and/or public service. The intent of the Instructional Staff category is to include all individuals whose primary occupation includes instruction at the institution. Instruction (only) - Persons whose specific assignments customarily are made for the purpose of providing instruction or teaching. Regardless of title, academic rank, or tenure status, these employees formally spend the majority of their time providing instruction or teaching. Instruction combined with research and/or public service (IRPS) - Persons for whom it is not possible to differentiate between instruction or teaching, research, and public service because each of these functions is an integral component of his/her regular assignment. Regardless, of title, academic rank, or tenure status, these employees formally spend the majority of their time providing instruction, research, and/or public service. Full-time staff (employees) As defined by the institution. The type of appointment at the snapshot date determines whether an employee is full-time or part-time. The employee's term of contract is not considered in making the determination of full- or part-time. A status designated by the institution according to the institution's policies. The IPEDS HR survey includes the ranks of Professor, Associate Professor, Assistant Professor, Instructor, and Lecturer.

tabletitle: Number and salary outlays for full-time nonmedical instructional staff, by gender, and academic rank: Academic year 2015-16
description: This table contains the number of full-time, nonmedical, instructional staff by academic rank, contract length and gender and salary outlays by academic rank and gender. Number of staff are reported by 9-, 10-, 11- and 12-month contracts by academic rank. Total number of months covered by all staff are generated. Total salary outlays by academic rank are then divided by the total months covered by academic rank to generate a weighted average monthly salary for each academic rank and gender. description: This table contains the number of staff, total salary outlays and average salaries of full-time, nonmedical, instructional staff by academic rank, number of months worked, and gender. The categories for number of months worked are 9-, 10-, 11- and 12-months. Number of staff working less than 9 months are also available, but salary data are not available for this group. Equated 9-month salary outlays and equated 9-month average salaries are also available by academic rank and gender. For details see the variables listed in the vartable16 tab. This data file has multiple records for each institution. Each record is uniquely defined by the variables IPEDS ID (UNITID), and the variable academic rank (ARANK) of full-time instructional staff. Between 2012 and 2015 salary information were not available by number of months worked. Equated 9-month average salaries were available, but because of the lack of detailed salary data by the number of months worked, it is not consistent with equated 9-month salary data generated in 2016. Prior to 2012, number of staff and salary information were available for 9/10 months worked and 11/12 months worked. Equated 9-month average salaries and equated 9-month salary outlays were available and is more consistent with the 2016 equated salaries. Prior to 2016 the number of months worked were referred to as contract lengths. In 2016, the salary survey collection screens used the "number of months worked" terminology.

tabletitle: Total entering class, retention rates, and student-to-faculty ratio: Fall 2015
description: This table contains data on the total entering class, first-year retention rates and the student-to-faculty ratio. The total entering class are the number of incoming students (students enrolling for the first time in a postsecondary institution versus students transferring in from another postsecondary institution) at an institution. This measure permits the calculation of the graduation rate cohort as a proportion of the total entering student body. The first-year retention rate data measures the percentage of first-year students who had persisted in or completed their educational program a year later (began in fall 2014 and persisted or completed in fall 2015). Student-to-faculty ratio is defined as total FTE students not in graduate or professional programs divided by total FTE instructional staff not teaching in graduate or professional programs. All data in this table are applicable only to institutions with undergraduate students. Institutions with traditional academic year calendar systems (semester, quarter, trimester or 4-1-4) report their enrollment as of October 15 or the official fall reporting date of the institution (academic year). Institutions with calendar systems that differ by program or allow continuous enrollment, report students that are enrolled at any time between August 1 and October 31 (program year). Only academic year institutions report entering class data. Institutions with short programs (less-than-one-year) will not have data on retention.

longdescription: Student-to-faculty ratio - Total FTE students not in graduate or professional programs divided by total FTE instructional staff not teaching in graduate or professional programs. Total FTE students is equal to the number of full-time students plus 1/3 the number of part-time students (Fall enrollment component). Graduate or first-professional students enrolled in graduate or professional programs such as medicine, law, veterinary, dentistry, social work, or public health, in which faculty teach virtually only graduate-level students (often referred to as "stand-alone" or "independent" programs) are excluded from both full-time and part-time counts. Total FTE instructional staff is equal to the number of full-time instructional staff to 1/3 the number of part-time instructional staff (Human Resource Component, EAP section). Instructional staff include employees whose primary function/occupational activity is primarily instruction or instruction/research/public service and are not medical school employees. Instructional staff teaching in graduate or professional programs such as medicine, law, veterinary, dentistry, social work, or public health, in which faculty teach virtually only graduate-level students (often referred to as "stand-alone" or "independent" programs) are excluded from both full-time and part-time counts.

  Example fields: Level of student; Grand total; Total men; Total women.
- **Race/ethnicity, gender, attendance status, and level of student**.  
  Example fields: Level of student; U.S. Nonresident men; U.S. Nonresident women; Race/ethnicity unknown men.
- **Major field of study, race/ethnicity, gender, attendance status, and level of student: Fall2022** — Reporting periods: Fall 2022.  
  Example fields: Major field of study; U.S. Nonresident men; U.S. Nonresident women; Race/ethnicity unknown men.
- **Major field of study, race/ethnicity, gender, attendance status, and level of student** — Reporting periods: Fall 2016; Fall 2018; Fall 2020; Fall 2024.  
  Example fields: Major field of study; U.S. Nonresident men; U.S. Nonresident women; Race/ethnicity unknown men.
- **Age category, gender, attendance status, and level of student** — Reporting periods: Fall 2023.  
  Example fields: Age category; Original line number on survey form; Level of student; Full time men.
- **Age category, gender, attendance status, and level of student: Fall 2015 (optional)** — Reporting periods: Fall 2015.

- **Age category, gender, attendance status, and level of student: Fall 2016 (optional)** — Reporting periods: Fall 2016.

- **Age category, gender, attendance status, and level of student: Fall 2017 (optional)** — Reporting periods: Fall 2017.

Includes name, address, city, state, zip code and various URL links to the institution's home page, admissions, financial aid offices and the net price calculator. Identifies institutions as currently active, institutions that participate in Title IV federal financial aid programs for which IPEDS is mandatory. It also includes variables derived from the 2023-24 Institutional Characteristics survey, such as control and level of institution, highest level and highest degree offered and Carnegie classifications.
release: Provisional/final (institutions are not allowed to revise these data)
release date: September 2025

vartitle: Sector of institution
datatype: N
fieldwidth: 2
format: Disc
multirecord: 0
filenumber: 1
sectionnumber: 2
longdescription: One of nine institutional categories resulting from dividing the universe according to control and level. Control categories are public, private not-for-profit, and private for-profit. Level categories are 4-year and higher (4 year), 2-but-less-than 4-year (2 year), and less than 2-year. For example: public, 4-year institutions. Control - A classification of whether an institution is operated by publicly elected or appointed officials (public control) or by privately elected or appointed officials and derives its major source of funds from private sources (private control). Level - A classification of whether an institution’s programs are 4-year or higher (4 year), 2-but-less-than 4-year (2 year), or less than 2-year.
varsource: IPEDS, Fall 2024, Institutional Characteristics Header component
